Decision_Topic: Training Epoch Budget & Checkpoint Selection Procedure
Available_Options: Option 1: 15 Epochs with Max Validation Mean Dice checkpointing on 155-case validation pool; Option 2: Checkpoint on 50-case Val_cal only; Option 3: Final epoch (Epoch 15) checkpointing
Recommended_Choice: Option 1: 15 Epochs with Max Validation Mean Dice checkpointing on 155-case validation pool with mandatory disclosure of selection exposure
Technical_Rationale: Preserves exact training parity with Stage B. Evaluates validation Mean Dice across all 3 tumor classes at epoch end. Crucially: because all 105 Val_eval cases and 50 Val_cal cases are part of the 155-case pool, both cohorts are selection-exposed to checkpoint selection. Results on Val_eval must be formally reported as selection-exposed internal validation, not independent evaluation.
Risk_If_Unresolved: Failing to disclose checkpoint-selection overlap misrepresents selection-exposed internal validation as independent evaluation; checkpointing on Val_cal introduces protocol divergence against Stage B baselines.
Status: APPROVED (2026-11-13) — Use the approved 15-epoch checkpoint-selection procedure

Available_Options: Option 1: Strict random scratch initialization for all 5 models; Option 2: Hybrid initialization (ImageNet pretrained encoder for UNetResNet34, scratch for others with explicit disclosure)
Recommended_Choice: Option 2: Hybrid initialization with mandatory architectural disclosure in all tables and reports
Technical_Rationale: UNetResNet34 was specifically designed to evaluate whether transfer learning from ImageNet improves medical feature extraction. Forcing scratch initialization eliminates the core architectural distinction under test.
Risk_If_Unresolved: Conflating pretrained and scratch models without explicit disclosure invalidates fair scientific comparison; forcing scratch destroys transfer learning research objective.

Decision_Topic: Axial-Context Window Radius Parameter & Fallback Policy
Available_Options: Option 1: k=2 (radius 2, window of 5 slices [z-2 to z+2]) with empty-prediction fallback; Option 2: k=1 (radius 1); Option 3: Uncertainty-gated fallback (tau_fb=0.40)
Primary_Evidence: src/agent/state.py line 69, src/agent/runner.py line 93, tools/demo_app.py, tools/reevaluate_missing_modality_policy.py lines 180-191
Recommended_Choice: Option 1: k=2 (radius 2, inspecting up to 4 neighboring axial slices within case) with empty-prediction fallback
Technical_Rationale: k=2 is the actual implemented and executed parameter across Milestone 5 Option A, Gate 6A, November 10 B2 evaluation, and the Streamlit showcase. Canonical B2 fallback is triggered strictly by empty primary prediction with axial support; tau_fb=0.40 was unexecuted in B2.
Risk_If_Unresolved: Discrepancy between code (k=2) and documentation (r=1) creates audit contradictions; presenting unexecuted tau_fb=0.40 as canonical B2 policy misrepresents actual policy execution.

Available_Options: Option 1: Model-specific temperature scaling (T*_m) fitted on Val_cal, descriptive risk-coverage sweep tau in [0.05, 0.50] on Val_eval, with tau=0.35 as ResUNet reference point; Option 2: Assume global T*=2.8808 and tau=0.35 for all models
Recommended_Choice: Option 1: Model-specific temperature scaling fitted on Val_cal (selection-exposed internal subset); descriptive risk-coverage sweep tau in [0.05, 0.50] on Val_eval without post-hoc threshold selection
Technical_Rationale: T*=2.8808 and tau=0.35 are specific to ResUNet-2D (UNetResNet34 has T*=2.6267). Newly trained models produce distinct logit distributions and require independent T* optimization on Val_cal. Val_cal is selection-exposed to checkpoint selection; temperature fitting is calibration fitting on an internal subset. Sweeps on Val_eval are descriptive internal validation analyses; optimizing tau on Val_eval and claiming unbiased performance is strictly prohibited.
Risk_If_Unresolved: Assuming universal calibration parameters distorts ECE and selective prediction risk-coverage analysis; selecting operating thresholds on Val_eval and claiming unbiased performance violates validation integrity.

Available_Options: Option 1: Retain synthetic zero-clamping with corrected channel mapping (C3=T2f, C4=T2w) and add direct compartment failure cross-tabulation; Option 2: Discard missing modality study; Option 3: Retrain models with modality dropout
Recommended_Choice: Option 1: Retain synthetic zero-clamping with corrected channel mapping and add direct compartment failure cross-tabulation
Technical_Rationale: Discovered critical failure mode (predictive entropy fails to signal Enhancing Tumor collapse under missing T1c). Correcting labels and directly cross-tabulating slice failure (Dice < 0.5) against triage action proves that uncertainty cannot replace input validation gates.

Decision_Topic: Statistical Unit of Analysis & Multiple Testing Correction
Available_Options: Option 1: Patient/Subject level (primary) with case-level secondary reporting; Holm-Bonferroni FWER control for pairwise models; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR for exploratory metrics; authoritative slice reporting; Option 2: Slice-level pooling without FWER control
Recommended_Choice: Option 1: Patient/Subject level aggregation; Holm-Bonferroni FWER for pairwise tests; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR for exploratory analysis; authoritative slice accounting (16,275 raw, 8,382 filtered, 6,549 foreground)
Technical_Rationale: Patient-level aggregation prevents inflated degrees of freedom from spatially correlated slices. Holm-Bonferroni strictly controls FWER across 10 pairwise model comparisons; Benjamini-Hochberg controls FDR for exploratory compartment metrics. Slice frames are rigorously categorized into raw (16,275), background-filtered (8,382), and foreground (6,549).
Risk_If_Unresolved: Slice-level statistical testing violates the i.i.d. assumption; conflating FWER and FDR leads to peer review rejection; slice count ambiguities cause reporting contradictions.
